title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page. Let A be a ring of characteristic p and B a truncated one-variable algebra: on the previous page (p>3), B = A[T]/(T^p - α). Let D^{(i)} = ∂_t^{(i)} be the divided-power (Hasse) derivations. For a 'coordinate' s ∈ B, with D^{(1)}s a unit, Grothendieck considers the quantity c_0(s) = D^{(3)}s·D^{(1)}s − (D^{(2)}s)^2. Over Q this equals (1/6)(s's''' − (3/2)s''^2) = (s'^2/6)·{s,t}, so it is a characteristic-free normalisation of the Schwarzian derivative.

The claim is a local rigidity statement: c_0(s)=0 forces s to be a Möbius (homographic) transform of t. The argument runs as follows.
- Reduce to α=0.
- Normalise by affine maps s ↦ a_1^{-1}(s−a_0), so that s = t + a_2t^2 + ….
- Apply the Möbius change s ↦ s/(1+a_2 s), so that s ≡ t mod t^3.
- It remains to show that if s = t + a t^d + (order > d) with d ≥ 3, then a = 0.
- Comparing lowest-order terms of c_0(s) gives a·C(d,3)·t^{d−3} ≡ 0 mod t^{d−2}, hence a·C(d,3) = 0.
- For p>3 and 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1, C(d,3) is invertible, so a = 0.

This page: characteristic 2 and 3. Here a third divided derivative is meaningless on a ring of length p ≤ 3. So one must take B = A[T]/(T^{p^2} − α), with the definition of the ∂^{(i)} suitably rectified. The commutative-algebra statement and the reduction to α=0, s ≡ t mod t^3, are as before. One must show a = 0 for s = t + a t^d, 3 ≤ d ≤ p^2 − 1.

The same identity a·C(d,3) = 0 holds, written a·c_{3,d−3} = 0 with c_{i,j} = C(i+j,i). By Lucas/Kummer, c_{3,d−3} ∈ F_p^* iff adding 3 and d−3 in base p has no carry. Writing d−3 = d_0 + d_1 p and 3 = d'_0 + d'_1 p, this means d_0 + d'_0 ≤ p−1 and d_1 + d'_1 ≤ p−1.
- p=2: the only d in range is d=3, the coefficient is 1, so a = 0.
- p=3: after a crossed-out false start, 3 = 0 + 1·3. Since 0 ≤ d−3 ≤ 5 we have d_1 ≤ 1, and the condition reduces to d_1 + 1 ≤ 2, which always holds. So a = 0 ('On gagne encore!').

Upshot: in every characteristic, on the p-adically appropriate Frobenius neighbourhood (length p for p>3, length p^2 for p=2,3), the solutions of the divided-power Schwarzian equation are exactly the Möbius transforms of t. This is a local uniqueness lemma for (Frobenius-)projective structures in characteristic p, in the context of the Cartier operator.
errors: For p=2 the coefficient written c_{3,3}=1 should read c_{3,0} = C(3,3) = 1 (with d=3, d−3=0); a notational slip, harmless.
The crossed-out p=3 attempt computes c_{d,d−3}, the wrong index pattern, and the case analysis there is confused; Grothendieck abandons it and redoes it correctly with c_{3,d−3}.

The 'rectification de la définition des ∂^{(i)}' for B = A[T]/(T^{p^2} − α) with α ≠ 0 is left unspecified. Divided-power derivations on A[T]/(T^{p^2} − α) exist only after suitable care (e.g. reduction to α=0 or working étale-locally). This is a gap in the text, though the reduction to α=0 makes it inessential.

Implicitly, the induction on the lowest-order term needs D^{(1)}s ≡ 1 mod t^{d−1}, which holds after normalisation. The argument is otherwise correct; I verified C(d,3) mod 3 ≠ 0 for d=3..8 (values 1,4,10,20,35,56).

ideas.what: Characteristic-free Schwarzian c_0(s) = D^{(3)}s·D^{(1)}s − (D^{(2)}s)^2 using Hasse/divided derivatives, and the lemma that its vanishing characterises Möbius transforms of t on a truncated (Frobenius-neighbourhood) algebra
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative in positive characteristic / local uniqueness for F-projective (Frobenius-projective) structures, dormant PGL_2-opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Schwarzian equations in char p, 1970s); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, dormant indigenous bundles, 1990s); Hoshi and Wakabayashi (Frobenius-projective structures, higher-level dormant opers, 2010s–2020s)

ideas.what: Need to pass from length p to length p^2 truncation (T^{p^2}) in characteristic 2 and 3 so that third divided derivatives make sense, with a Lucas-theorem check of invertibility of C(d,3)
Normalisation of a coordinate by affine plus homographic change s ↦ s/(1+a_2 s) to kill the quadratic term
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2 jet normalisation (3-jet transitivity of Möbius group)

missed.claim: In notes on Gauss–Manin connections and the Cartier operator, Grothendieck works out a characteristic-free (divided-power) Schwarzian and proves that its zeros on the Frobenius neighbourhood are exactly Möbius transforms. He also notices that in characteristic 2 and 3 one must enlarge to the p^2-th Frobenius neighbourhood. This is essentially the local lemma underlying the theory of (dormant) projective structures/opers and higher-level F^N-projective structures in characteristic p, developed decades later (Ihara, Mochizuki, Hoshi, Wakabayashi) without reference to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Cas car. 2 ou 3. Ici il faut supposer B = A[T]/(T^{p^2}-α) ... La condition c_{3,d-3}∈F_p^* signifie donc d_1+1≤p-1 ... On gagne encore!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck linked Cartier-operator/Frobenius-descent questions to projective structures in characteristic p, including the small primes 2 and 3 often excluded in the later literature (Mochizuki typically assumes p odd). His p^2-truncation treatment of p=2,3 is a concrete precursor of higher-level (F^2-) projective structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is elementary (Lucas theorem). But the context, a Schwarzian/Möbius rigidity lemma on Frobenius neighbourhoods with a level-2 fix for p=2,3 inside Cartier-operator notes, anticipates themes of dormant opers and Frobenius-projective structures that are credited to later authors. It is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major result.
transcription_corrections: 's ≡ t (∂^3 B)' is likely 's ≡ t mod (t^3 B)', i.e. mod t^3.
'c_{3,3}=1' in the p=2 case should be understood as c_{3,0} (d=3).
In the crossed-out p=3 block, 'c_{d,d-3} = c_{d_0,d_0} c_{d_1,d_1-1}' is Grothendieck's own abandoned (incorrect) attempt, not a transcription error.
Right column: '(d varie 0≤d-3≤5 i.e. 0≤d_1≤1 car 3≤d≤p^2−1=8)' is correctly read; '3 = 0 + 1·p' was corrected in the original from a different first digit.
